bottom_line: In men with moderate hypercholesterolemia and no history of myocardial infarction, pravastatin vs placebo reduced the risk of definite nonfatal myocardial infarction or death from coronary heart disease by 31% (95% confidence interval, 17 to 43 percent).
implications: These data support that, over about 5 years, pravastatin compared with placebo reduced definite nonfatal myocardial infarction or death from coronary heart disease (248 (7.9) vs 174 (5.5); risk reduction 31% (17 to 43); P<0.001). They also show a reduction in death from all cardiovascular causes (73 (2.3) vs 50 (1.6); 32% (3 to 53); P=0.033) and no statistically significant difference in death from noncardiovascular causes (62 (1.9) vs 56 (1.7); P=0.54). The document does not establish a statistically significant reduction in death from any cause (P=0.051) and does not show a difference in fatal or nonfatal stroke (P=0.57).

harms.text: Incident cancers: 116 in pravastatin group vs 106 in placebo group (P=0.55).

In the pravastatin group 116 subjects had incident
(fatal or nonfatal) cancers, as compared with 106 in the
placebo group (P 0.55).

harms.text: Myalgia reported by 20 subjects in the pravastatin group vs 19 in the placebo group; muscle aches 97 vs 102 (P not significant).
harms.quote:
Twenty subjects
in the pravastatin group reported myalgia, and 97 mus-
cle aches. The corresponding numbers in the placebo
group were 19 and 102 (P not signiﬁcant).

harms.text: Elevations in aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase values (≥3 times upper reference limits): 26 and 16 in pravastatin vs 20 and 12 in placebo (P not significant).

harms.text: Fatal or nonfatal stroke: 46 in the pravastatin group (6 fatal) vs 51 in the placebo group (4 fatal).
